findings.title: Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot's date matches a date override, checkIfIsAvailable sets dateOverrideExist and returns true at lines 133-135 before reaching the busy.every() check at line 153. Therefore a fixed (or round-robin) host who has a calendar/Cal booking overlapping a slot on an override day is reported available for that slot, so overlapping bookings can be created precisely on override days.

findings.title: Empty (unavailable-day) override check compares Dayjs objects with ===
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false. An override with start == end, used to mark a whole day unavailable, is therefore never detected as such; slots at/after that instant fall through, have dateOverrideExist=true, and are returned as available instead of being blocked for the day.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots covered by any one of multiple ranges and ignores slot end
findings.body: The code uses find() for any workingHour on that weekday where the slot start is before its startTime or after its endTime, and sets both start and end from the slot start (lines 141-142, so eventLength is never checked). With split availability on one day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00) a 09:00 slot matches the second range as 'outside' and is rejected, while a slot starting inside a range but ending after it ends is accepted. This breaks fixed-host filtering for users with split or multiple same-day ranges.

findings.title: Override conversion assumes timeZone is present and loses day-boundary crossing
findings.body: TimeRange.timeZone is optional (added as timeZone? in schedule.d.ts) and other getSlots callers need not supply it, yet lines 212-213 unconditionally call .tz(override.timeZone); with undefined this does not give the organizer offset. Additionally lines 218-223 reduce the shifted start/end to hour*60+minute, discarding the date: an override shifted by the invitee/organizer offset across midnight produces endTime <= startTime (or a time belonging to the adjacent invitee day), which buildSlots discards via start >= end, so those override slots disappear instead of appearing on the correct day.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host override fix
findings.body: The PR description claims fixed hosts' date overrides are now honoured for round-robin events, but the only added test (lines 788-804) re-queries the existing single-user date-override scenario in Asia/Dhaka and asserts identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with an override and a non-fixed host, nor an unavailable/empty override or a busy time on an override day, so the new checkIfIsAvailable filtering path for fixed hosts is untested and regressions in it would not be caught.
